sections.title: Telling the Time
sections.content: The clock runs on 'ser' and on 'las', because the hours are feminine: 'son las diez'. One o'clock is the only singular — 'es la una'. To say when something happens, swap 'son' for 'a': 'el museo abre a las nueve'. Add 'de la mañana', 'de la tarde' or 'de la noche' when it is not obvious which nine you mean.

sections.title: At what time?
rows: a las nueve de la mañana
a las cinco de la tarde

items.spanish: El museo abre a las nueve y cierra a las cinco.
items.english: The museum opens at nine and closes at five.

items.spanish: ¿A qué hora quieres ir? A las diez.
items.english: What time do you want to go? At ten.

items.spanish: A las nueve y media salen de casa.
items.english: At half past nine they leave the house.

items.spanish: El autobús pasa cada veinte minutos.
items.english: The bus comes every twenty minutes.

sections.content: 'Son las diez' tells you the time; 'a las diez' tells you when something happens. Getting these two mixed up is the usual slip: '¿A qué hora abre?' — 'Abre a las nueve', never 'Abre son las nueve'.

sections.topic: the verb 'ser', which Spanish uses for the time
